title: Deterministic Bytecode Comparison (V2.7)
description: Reference shape for scripts/compare_bytecode.py's output record (docs/decisiones.md D-057). This script NEVER makes a network call and NEVER modifies preprocess.py, score.py, registry.py, detectors/ or systemGraph. It compares source-compiled bytecode vs deployed runtime bytecode, constructor/deployed vs runtime, and proxy implementation source vs runtime. Verdicts are strictly MATCH, MISMATCH, UNAVAILABLE, INCOMPLETE, UNRESOLVED. MISMATCH is a technical fact, never an automatic vulnerability finding.

compareVersion.description: Version identifier of the bytecode comparison module (e.g. '2026.1').

address.description: Lowercase-normalized address of the primary analyzed contract, or null if unresolvable.

network.description: Network identification as chainId, canonical name, or network object.

verified.description: Whether the source code is verified. Evaluated by identity (is True), never bool()-coerced.

proxyComparisons.description: Per-proxy implementation comparisons derived from systemGraph.proxies[].

capabilityChecks.description: V2.8 Block 2/3 (C-01/C-05/C-07). One entry per chains.py-tracked EVM capability (supportsPush0, supportsTransientStorage, supportsCancun/MCOPY): whether the opcode is actually used in the scanned bytecode and, if so, whether the target chain's catalog supports it. UNAVAILABLE covers both 'no bytecode to scan' and 'chain unknown/uncataloged' - the latter is this script's equivalent of NOT_ASSESSED (compatibility could not be evaluated, never assumed compatible).

compilerVersionCheck.description: V2.8 Block 2 (C-02). Explorer-reported compilerVersion vs the solc version byte-encoded in runtimeBytecode's own CBOR metadata trailer (reuses the existing CBOR boundary detection; a scoped decoder, not a general CBOR parser). Gated on verified (D-060): verified is not True yields UNAVAILABLE, mirroring sourceVsRuntime's trust gate (D-056) - an unverified record's explorer-reported compilerVersion is never compared as if trustworthy. A MISMATCH is a data-integrity/provenance fact about explorer metadata, never a vulnerability signal.

crossChainImplementationDrift.description: V2.8 Block 2 (C-03), corrected in D-060, extended in D-061 (C-10/C-14). When 2+ RESOLVED proxies on DIFFERENT chains delegate to implementations that share a reliable, content-based identity (the CBOR-embedded source metadata hash - ipfs/bzzr - Solidity's own compiler emits; reuses C-02's decoder), compares their runtime bytecode after CBOR normalization. Bare contract name and address are NEVER used to group candidates (D-060: bare-name grouping was removed after it was found to false-group unrelated same-named contracts). An implementation whose metadata identity cannot be established contributes no comparison. Empty for single-chain deployments or when no reliable identity exists. A MISMATCH item additionally carries 'divergenceProfile' (C-10): a PURELY DESCRIPTIVE byte-diff characterization against a reference chain - it NEVER changes the verdict and NEVER constitutes a finding by itself (R-C2 still governs interpretation). Every item carries 'chainsKnown' (C-14), also purely descriptive.

chainsKnown.description: C-14. chainId -> whether it is in chains.py's known catalog. Descriptive only - never blocks or changes the comparison.

divergenceProfile.description: C-10, MISMATCH items only. Descriptive only - never a verdict, never a finding.

perChain.description: One entry per OTHER chain whose bytecode differs from the reference; a chain matching the reference is simply omitted.

crossChainProvenanceConsistency.description: V2.8 Block 3 (C-09), extended in Block 4 (C-12/C-14). For implementations already grouped by crossChainImplementationDrift's reliable metadata identity, whether caller-supplied verifiedMap/compilerVersionMap/contractNameMap (optional rawInput fields, parallel to sourceBytecodeMap/runtimeBytecodeMap) agree across chains. A disagreement is a provenance/integrity fact, never a vulnerability signal (same discipline as C-04) - contractName disagreement in particular is integrity metadata only, never itself evidence of anything malicious. Empty when none of the three maps is supplied - never falls back to the single primary record's own top-level verified/compilerVersion/contractName field.

disagreements.description: Present keys are 'verified', 'compilerVersion', and/or 'contractName' (C-12), each mapping chainId to the disagreeing value; empty object when nothing disagrees.

chainsKnown.description: C-14. chainId -> whether it is in chains.py's known catalog. Descriptive only.

crossChainProxyDrift.description: V2.8 Block 4 (C-11). Same mechanism as crossChainImplementationDrift (C-03), grouped on the PROXY's own key/bytecode instead of the implementation's - proxies are expected to be structurally stable across a multi-chain rollout, so drift here is at least as strong a signal. Never a vulnerability signal. Carries the same divergenceProfile (C-10) and chainsKnown (C-14) fields as crossChainImplementationDrift.

chainsKnown.description: C-14. chainId -> whether it is in chains.py's known catalog. Descriptive only.

divergenceProfile.description: C-10, MISMATCH items only. Descriptive only - never a verdict, never a finding.

crossChainCoverageSummary.description: V2.8 Block 4 (C-13). Purely descriptive aggregation over the SAME resolved-proxy population crossChainImplementationDrift/crossChainProxyDrift already group - adds no new detection logic and never affects any verdict. Surfaces how many resolved proxies/implementations had no reliable identity to compare with (previously invisible).

limitations.description: Technical limitations and non-MATCH comparison findings propagated for contextual AI interpretation.

note.description: Fixed legal/methodological disclaimer restating that non-MATCH verdicts are technical facts, never automatic findings.

rawInput.description: Extended V2.6.1 ingestion record consumed by compare_bytecode.py. Contains V2.6.1 fields plus optional bytecode and systemGraph fields.

network.description: Chain id, network name, or object.

runtimeBytecodeMap.description: Keyed by systemGraph key. May contain implementation keys (C-03/C-09/C-02's proxy comparisons) AND/OR proxy keys (V2.8 Block 4, C-11) - the same map serves both, no separate field.

verifiedMap.description: V2.8 Block 3 (C-09). Optional, keyed like runtimeBytecodeMap.

compilerVersionMap.description: V2.8 Block 3 (C-09). Optional, keyed like runtimeBytecodeMap.

contractNameMap.description: V2.8 Block 4 (C-12). Optional, keyed like runtimeBytecodeMap.

coverageBucket.description: C-13 per-target-type coverage counts. withIdentityCount + withoutIdentityCount == the parent resolvedProxyCount.

businessRules: R-C1: Verdicts are strictly MATCH, MISMATCH, UNAVAILABLE, INCOMPLETE, UNRESOLVED. No other verdict codes are permitted.
R-C2: MISMATCH is never an automatic vulnerability finding or security signal; it is a technical fact recorded in comparisons and limitations.
R-C3: CBOR metadata stripping is deterministic, stdlib-only, requiring len >= 4, declared length > 0 and < len - 2, and fixmap marker 0xa0..0xb7.
R-C4: Constructor args separated via runtime prefix or elementary static ABI types; non-elementary types or missing data yield INCOMPLETE without guessing lengths.
R-C5: Proxy comparisons read systemGraph.proxies[]; unresolved proxies stay UNRESOLVED; proxy != implementation is not a mismatch by itself.
R-C6: Zero network/RPC calls; stdlib only; never modifies preprocess.py, score.py, registry.py, detectors/, or systemGraph.

R-C7: capabilityChecks scans bytecode for actual opcode presence (a linear opcode walk that correctly skips PUSH-data bytes, never a substring search) - never inferred from source text or compiler version alone.
R-C8: An unknown/uncataloged chain for capabilityChecks always yields UNAVAILABLE, never MATCH - absence of a capability warning must never be read as 'compatible'.

R-C9: compilerVersionCheck's CBOR decoding is scoped ONLY to the short definite-length map/text-string/byte-string encodings Solidity's own metadata encoder emits - any other encoding yields INCOMPLETE, never a guessed version.

R-C10: crossChainImplementationDrift groups candidates ONLY by a reliable, content-based identity (the CBOR-embedded ipfs/bzzr metadata hash) and only across DIFFERENT chains - bare contract name and address are never used to group candidates, and an implementation whose identity cannot be established never contributes a comparison (D-060).

R-C11: compilerVersionCheck only compares when verified is True; verified is not True (false, absent, or any non-boolean) yields UNAVAILABLE without inspecting compilerVersion or runtimeBytecode, mirroring sourceVsRuntime's trust gate (D-056/D-060).
R-C12: capabilityChecks' MCOPY/supportsCancun entry follows the exact same rules as PUSH0/supportsTransientStorage (R-C7/R-C8) - byte-level opcode walk, unknown chain always UNAVAILABLE, never MATCH.

R-C13: crossChainProvenanceConsistency only compares implementations already grouped by crossChainImplementationDrift's reliable metadata identity - it never independently re-derives or infers a cross-chain relationship from name/address, and never falls back to the single primary record's own verified/compilerVersion field for a group it does not belong to.

R-C14: divergenceProfile (crossChainImplementationDrift MISMATCH items only) is purely descriptive and MUST NEVER change the verdict or be treated as a finding by itself; 'localized' is never a claim about the actual cause (immutables, linked libraries, or a genuine change are all indistinguishable from raw bytes alone).

R-C15: crossChainProxyDrift uses the identical mechanism and verdict rules as crossChainImplementationDrift (R-C10/R-C14), grouped on the proxy key instead of the implementation key - never a vulnerability signal.
R-C16: contractName disagreement in crossChainProvenanceConsistency is integrity metadata only - it MUST NEVER be worded or treated as a vulnerability/security claim.

R-C17: crossChainCoverageSummary is purely descriptive aggregation with no verdict field and MUST NEVER affect any comparison's outcome - it only counts, never explains why an entry lacks an identity.

R-C18: chainsKnown (on crossChainImplementationDrift/crossChainProvenanceConsistency/crossChainProxyDrift items) is purely descriptive and MUST NEVER block or alter a comparison - an unknown chain's bytecode/metadata is still compared identically; a broken chains.json catalog degrades every entry to false rather than aborting the comparison.
